# Lockheed delivered 110 F-35s in 2025 as TR-3 software backlog cleared

Breaking Defense, January 15, 2026

Lockheed Martin delivered 110 F-35 aircraft in 2025, the company said, after the Technology Refresh 3 software issue that held jets in storage through 2024 was resolved. The company has said it expects 2026 deliveries of 170 to 190 aircraft as parked jets are released to customers.

The F-35 competes for export orders against Boeing's F-15EX and, in Europe, against the Eurofighter Typhoon and Dassault Rafale. Boeing has positioned the F-15EX as a lower-cost complement for air forces that already operate the F-15, while Lockheed argues the F-35's sensor fusion and stealth justify its higher unit price.

Lockheed also noted that the F-16 Block 70/72 line in Greenville, South Carolina delivered 24 aircraft in 2025, and that the C-130J remains in production for the U.S. Air Force and international customers.
